title: Printable Map with Scale Context: Print True
description: Prepare a Printable Map with Scale Context for classroom or field printouts — scale bars that survive printing, framing that respects the paper. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a field class prints a 1:50,000 sheet where the scale bar says 1 cm is 500 metres — and because it is printed at 100%, the bar is telling the truth.
quick_answer: The Printable Map with Scale Context page helps you prepare maps for paper — classroom sheets and field printouts — where a printed scale bar still means what it says. Frame the area, set the scale context, and print at true size so distances measured with a ruler stay honest.

Printed maps at meetings get measured on by pencils and fingers. A correct scale bar is the difference between a discussion and an argument afterwards.
Paper records outlive platforms. A scale-true print with its date and source noted is a document; a screenshot is a rumour.

A teacher prints at 'fit to page' — the sheet shrinks 6%, and every student's ruler answer is 6% short. The fix is one setting: print at 100% (actual size), and verify with the scale bar before the class measures anything.
A 1:50,000 bar reads 1 cm = 500 m along its metric face; the same sheet's inch is 1.27 km of ground. Good printouts serve both rulers — this page frames for that.

popular_table.note: These truths hold only at 100% print size on the stated paper. 'Fit', 'shrink to printable area' and photocopier scaling all quietly rewrite the scale — the printed bar, re-measured with a ruler, is the only witness that counts.

faq: Which paper size should I choose?

Match the printer the sheet will actually meet: A4 in most of Europe, Letter in the US. A map framed for one and printed on the other gets margins cropped or the whole sheet scaled — the trap this page exists to prevent.
Why does my scale bar disagree with my ruler?
Something rescaled the page: a fit-to-page setting, a driver default, or a photocopier. Reprint at 100%/actual size and re-measure the bar before trusting any distance taken from the sheet.
Can I print in black and white?
Yes — outline-style maps print cleanly in greyscale and photocopy well. Check that any colour coding still reads as distinct greys before printing fifty copies.
How do I add a north arrow and title?
Frame and export the map image, then finish the furniture — title, north arrow, date, source line — in your document or slides tool where typography is controllable. Record copies deserve all four.
What resolution should the export be?
Enough that lines stay crisp at the paper size: export at the largest framing offered and avoid enlarging beyond it. A slightly smaller map printed sharp beats a bigger one printed fuzzy.
Can I laminate a printout and draw on it?
Field classic: laminate, mark with chinagraph or whiteboard pen, wipe, reuse. The scale bar under lamination stays true because the sheet beneath never changed size.
Is a printed map still accurate next year?
The scale stays true; the content ages. Roads and paths change — date your printouts and re-export for each season's fieldwork rather than trusting last year's sheet.
Can I print a satellite view with a scale bar?
Yes, if the framed view is the satellite basemap. The same rules apply — 100% size, verify the bar — because paper honesty is about printing, not imagery.
